subject: Draft customer story for BlueRidge — publish risk assessment
messages:
From: Aarti Shah <aarti.shah@blueridge-logistics.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Daniel Park <dpark@blueridge-logistics.com>, security@blueridge-logistics.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft customer story — quick read / sensitivity check

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for sending over the draft case study. I skimmed the doc and it looks good for a public-facing story, but I need to confirm a couple of internal things before we can be quoted on availability and incident detail. Specifically: 1) the timeline of the April incident in the support timeline — we had an internal post-mortem that revised some of the root-cause language; 2) our procurement team is still negotiating final language around data residency and logs.

Can you hold publishing until we confirm those two items? We really want this customer story to go live, but we have to avoid any statement that contradicts our compliance statements. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if that helps.

Best,
Aarti Shah
Head of Communications
BlueRidge Logistics

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Draft customer story — quick read / sensitivity check

Team — forwarding BlueRidge's note. They asked us to hold publication pending two confirmations (incident timeline + procurement language). Attached is the draft we shared and the support timeline (red flag in April).

Quick asks:
- Marissa — can comms adjust the quote to remove the specific "April" phrasing pending their confirmation?
- Vivek/Neha — any risk with leaving the case study under embargo until their procurement is done? Could this conflict with our campaign calendar?
- Jonas — pricing/terms note: do they have an active renewal within 90 days? If so, delaying might affect momentum.

I'll propose a short sync with Aarti if helpful.

Thanks,
Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: draft_case_study_v3.docx]
[Attachment: support_timeline.csv]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft customer story — quick read / sensitivity check

Thanks for flagging this, Mateo. I'm okay softening the date and moving any language that suggests a definitive root cause into a more generic paragraph. Suggested edits: replace "In April we experienced..." with "Following a service disruption, Redwood worked with BlueRidge to..." and remove the line that references log retention specifics.

However — per process, if they're asking us to withhold publication entirely until procurement signs off, we should honor that. The comms team can rework the opening and swap the quote for a less specific comms-friendly line.

I'll draft a revision and share v4 by EOD.

Marissa
Director, Marketing & Comms
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-publication-checklist.pdf]

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft customer story — quick read / sensitivity check

Appreciate the heads-up. My concern is two-fold: 1) blue-ridge is on a renewal conversation in late Oct (Jonas correct me if I'm off), and 2) procurement asking for data residency/logging language rarely blocks a case study forever but we should avoid committing to anything that could be interpreted as an SLA concession.

My recommendation: put the asset in embargo (internal approval only), tell Aarti we'll pause public publishing until they confirm, and ask them to provide a short confirmation email from procurement/security that the redactions are acceptable. If they refuse, we either publish a heavily redacted version or defer.

If we must delay >30 days, we should align with Sales for next steps (credits, co-marketing scheduling).

Vivek
VP, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 11:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft customer story — quick read / sensitivity check

Hi Aarti — thanks for the quick reply and for flagging procurement/security. We want to be good partners here and will not publish any contradictory statements. Proposed path forward:

1) We will embargo the customer story on our site and in campaign materials until you give explicit sign-off.
2) Marissa will produce a v4 draft that removes the specific April reference and replaces the root-cause wording with neutral language.
3) Could you ask procurement/security to provide a short confirmation email that the redacted wording is acceptable (copy to security@blueridge-logistics.com is fine)? That will help us move faster once you’re ready.

If it helps, we're happy to do a 20-min call Monday to walk through the edits.

Best,
Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Mateo — thanks for the quick turnaround and for being flexible. Procurement and InfoSec asked for the date language to be softened and to remove the explicit log retention sentence; they can provide a confirmation email early next week after a brief internal check. We agree to an embargo and will aim to get the confirmation by Wed, Sep 9.

We still want this story to go live — just want to make sure the published wording doesn't conflict with our external compliance statements. Appreciate the offer for a short call; let's hold off unless you need anything else.

Best,
Aarti
Head of Communications
BlueRidge Logistics
